questions.statement:
**What do you do when you open your eyes in the morning?**
*¿Qué haces cuando abres los ojos en la mañana?*
questions.explanation:
**Wake up** = open your eyes, stop sleeping. Different from "get up" (leave bed).
*Wake up = abrir los ojos, dejar de dormir. Diferente de "get up" (levantarse de la cama).*

**Morning Routine Vocabulary / Vocabulario de Rutina Matutina:**
| English | Español |
|---------|---------|
| Wake up | Despertarse |
| Get up | Levantarse |
| Brush teeth | Cepillarse los dientes |
| Take a shower | Ducharse |
| Get dressed | Vestirse |
| Have breakfast | Desayunar |

---

questions.statement: **What time should you arrive?** *¿A qué hora deberías llegar?*
questions.context: **Sign at school:** "Class starts at 7:30 AM. Please arrive 10 minutes early."
questions.explanation:
7:30 - 10 minutes = 7:20 AM. "Arrive early" = before the start time.
*7:30 - 10 minutos = 7:20 AM. "Arrive early" = antes de la hora de inicio.*

---

questions.context: **Mom:** "What time did you go to bed last night?"

options.text: Around 10 PM. I was finishing my science project. *(Alrededor de las 10 PM. Estaba terminando mi proyecto de ciencias.)*
Same as always. *(Lo mismo de siempre.)*

questions.explanation:
Good answers are specific (10 PM) and provide context (science project).
*Las buenas respuestas son específicas (10 PM) y dan contexto (proyecto de ciencias).*

---

questions.context: "I (1)______ breakfast every morning. Yesterday, I (2)______ eggs."
questions.explanation:
"Every morning" = habit = present simple (have). "Yesterday" = past simple (had).
*"Every morning" = hábito = presente simple. "Yesterday" = pasado simple.*

---

questions.statement: **What does the text say about study hours?**
questions.context: "Students in South Korea often study until midnight. In Finland, school days are shorter and there is less homework. Both countries have high education rankings, showing that more hours don't always equal better results."

options.text: More hours always mean better results.
Better results can be achieved without long study hours.
Only South Korea has good education.

questions.explanation:
"More hours don't always equal better results" = the text's main point.
*"Más horas no siempre significa mejores resultados" = el punto principal del texto.*

---

questions.statement: **What does this schedule suggest about the student's life?**
questions.context: "5:30 AM: Alarm rings. 6:00 AM: Bus arrives. 6:30 AM: First class. 3:00 PM: Sports practice. 6:00 PM: Homework. 9:00 PM: Finally, free time. 10:00 PM: Sleep. Repeat."

options.text: Their day is extremely structured with little free time.

questions.explanation:
"Finally, free time" at 9 PM + "Repeat" = busy, structured, limited rest.
*"Finally, free time" a las 9 PM + "Repeat" = ocupado, estructurado, descanso limitado.*

---

questions.context: "She (1)______ usually (2)______ TV in the morning."
questions.explanation:
"Usually" = present simple. She (3rd person) = doesn't + base verb.
*"Usually" = presente simple. She (3a persona) = doesn't + verbo base.*

---

options.text: Sleep longer than planned and wake up late

questions.explanation:
*Over-* = too much. "I overslept and missed class!" = slept too long.
*Over- = demasiado. "I overslept and missed class!" = dormí demasiado.*

---

questions.context: You have an exam tomorrow but you're too tired to study tonight.

options.text: Review key points briefly, sleep early, and wake up earlier to study.

questions.explanation:
Sleep helps memory! Brief review + good sleep = better than exhausted all-night studying.
*¡El sueño ayuda a la memoria! Repaso breve + buen sueño = mejor que estudiar agotado toda la noche.*

---

questions.context: **Quote:** "How you start your morning sets the tone for the rest of your day."

options.text: A good morning routine can positively affect your whole day.

questions.explanation:
"Sets the tone" = establishes the mood/energy. Good morning habits → productive day.
*"Sets the tone" = establece el ánimo/energía. Buenos hábitos matutinos → día productivo.*

questions.statement: **My brother is very _______. He is 1.90 meters!**

**English:** 1.90 meters is a description for someone who is "tall."
*Español: 1.90 metros es una descripción para alguien que es "tall" (alto).*

| English | Español |
|---------|---------|
| Tall | Alto |
| Short | Bajo/Pequeño |
| Curly hair | Cabello crespo |
| Straight hair | Cabello liso |

---

*Español: Usamos "has" (verbo tener) para "She/He/It" para describir rasgos físicos como el color de ojos o el cabello.*

---

questions.statement: **He always tells jokes. He is a _______ person.**
questions.explanation:
**English:** Someone who tells jokes is "funny."
*Español: Alguien que cuenta chistes es "funny" (gracioso).*

---

questions.context:
**Person A:** "What is your best friend like?"

*Español: "¿Cómo es alguien?" pregunta por la personalidad o descripción general.*

---

*Español: Usamos "are" para el sujeto "They" con adjetivos.*

---

questions.context: **Notice:** "Looking for a tall man, early 20s, wearing a red cap."

---

**English:** We use "are" for the subject "They."
